stem:
Yash looks at the diagram of a pentagon on a $1\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ grid. Dashed lines from one vertex split the pentagon into triangles. He wants the area of the pentagon in square centimetres.

Which claim correctly tells how to find that area?

options.text: Find the area of each triangle from the dashed split, then add those areas.
Report the word pentagon as the area on the grid.
Splitting into triangles is what creates the pentagon on the grid.
The area equals $1$ because the grid is labelled $1\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$.

teacher.key_rationale: Any polygon area is the sum of the areas of triangles that cover it without gaps or overlaps. Naming the shape, reversing cause, or grabbing the printed 1 all miss that reduction.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source grid quadrilateral as a pentagon on a 1 cm² grid with dashed splits into triangles.
